main_text.l: quod satis sit pro afferente, atque teste.
Quod salus hominum per homines est, cui
de hac scripserunt materia, vt nec
ipsas minutissimas ad illam spectantes præ-
De Purgatorio fuse egimus in notis ad
~5 letters] Sciul, seu Inferni intelligere tam
locum, in quo cruciantur Damnati æter-
num, quam eum, in quo animæ leuioribus
tamen ipsa eundem esse, ac Romanum
dictis, nomine [illegible, ~5 letters] Scial apud Chal-
dæos de solo loco, in quo animæ ad tempus

page.notes: The Arabic-script lines (the two lines of names and the Syriac/Arabic forms of Sciul and Scial) are not legible to me letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The Latin names beside them are transcribed as printed. The first Latin word "quod" in the first paragraph is italic. The page is continued from the previous page, hence cont="true". The word "stat" on the last line completes "con-" and stands beside the signature; I have joined it. The text is printed as "vbi", "vt" and "fusi-" with the original spelling retained, except for u/v and long s which are normalised as required.
